resources.title: Module 1: Linear structures (Synthetic)
resources.text: Module 1 (synthetic): linear structures. This synthetic lesson is written for automated tests and is not real course material. A stack is a last-in, first-out collection of elements. A queue is a first-in, first-out collection of elements. A deque is a double-ended queue that allows insertion and removal at both ends. Each list node holds 4 bytes, so 25 nodes use 25 * 4 = 100 bytes in total.

policy.evidence: Synthetic: AI help is allowed for practice in this synthetic course.

resources.title: Module 2: Hashing (Synthetic)
resources.text: Module 2 (synthetic): hashing. A hash function is a function that maps keys to bucket indexes. A collision is the event of two keys mapping to one bucket. Chaining is a method that stores colliding entries in a linked list. A table with 8 buckets and 3 keys per bucket holds 8 * 3 = 24 keys. The load factor is the number of stored keys divided by the number of buckets.

policy.evidence: Synthetic: AI help is allowed for practice in this synthetic course.

resources.title: Module 3: Running time (Synthetic)
resources.text: Module 3 (synthetic): running time. Big-O notation is a way to give an upper bound on the growth of a function. Binary search on 1024 sorted items needs at most 10 + 1 = 11 comparisons. A recurrence is an equation that defines a sequence in terms of its earlier values. Merge sort is a sorting algorithm that splits the input in half and merges the sorted halves.
